description: Semantic cases for the memory provenance and interpretation invariants. Each case is a candidate stored item described only in terms this checkpoint has actually fixed — origin, assertion kind, source reference, supersession target, owner — and never in terms of a table or column, because none exist yet. The validator decides allow or deny from the invariant set alone, so a future implementation inherits these decisions rather than reinventing them.

cases.title: A firsthand entry with a source reference is storable as a record
An AI summary cannot be stored as a record
cases.note: This is the single most important denial in the set. An AI summary stored as a record is indistinguishable from something the person wrote.

cases.title: An AI inference cannot be stored as a record
An AI summary is storable as an explicit AI view
cases.note: The product may hold model output. It may not hold it as the person's own words.

cases.title: Derived content without a source reference is refused
cases.note: Derived content that cannot name what it was derived from is unauditable and cannot be recomputed.

cases.title: A firsthand record without a source reference is refused
cases.note: Applies to every origin, including the account holder's own: without it, an injected record is indistinguishable from a captured one.

cases.title: A record cannot be superseded, only added to
cases.note: A correction is stored and linked; what it corrects stays readable. Marking the original superseded is a display decision, not a change to the original.

cases.title: A later interpretation may supersede an earlier interpretation
cases.note: 2022 'I want to stay', 2024 'I think I wanted to leave', 2026 'it was hard but not all bad' — all three persist, each dated to when it was held.

cases.title: An AI view cannot supersede something a person wrote
Supersession across accounts is refused
cases.note: Structurally impossible under the existing FORCE RLS predicates; asserted here so a future relation table inherits the same requirement rather than rediscovering it.

cases.title: Secondhand content cannot become the account holder's own record
cases.note: Restates INV-P0-013: what someone else said is their account, stored as such, not silently absorbed.

cases.title: Service history is storable as a record of what happened
cases.note: A track played at a time is a fact about behaviour. What it meant is not part of the record.

cases.title: An item carrying a life or importance score is refused
cases.note: Restates INV-P0-012 at the item level, so the prohibition survives into whatever the Memory domain becomes.

cases.title: An unremarkable record is as storable as any other
cases.note: A photo of a bowl of ramen on the way home. No field exists that could rank it below anything else, which is the point.

cases.title: Copies sharing one origin are one piece of evidence
cases.note: Three copies of one export are three artifacts and one origin. The current TrustScore contract would count three (GAP-MEM-002).

cases.title: Genuinely distinct origins do corroborate
cases.note: A photo the person took and a calendar entry are two origins. Corroboration is not forbidden; counting copies as corroboration is.

cases.title: A single permission cannot stand in for storage, search, analysis and resurfacing
cases.note: Deliberately denied even though no policy structure is defined yet. The one shape known to be wrong is a boolean, so it is refused before it can be built.

cases.title: Speaking as a person rather than citing the record is refused
cases.note: Restates INV-P0-018. Output about a person says what the record states, never what the person would say.
